Q: Repo state at a particular commit in VS Code A:

Open the "Source Control" sidebar tab. At the bottom of it (by default) is a pane entitled "Graph". Right-click on the commit you want and select "Checkout (Detached)".

To get back, click on the "..." in the "Changes" pane and select "Checkout To...". The entry bar at the top of the window will display a list of known branches and you can pick your default branch (often main).

The CLI equivalents of these are straightforward and well worth knowing: git checkout $COMMIT_ID or git switch --detach $COMMIT_ID to go into the past, git checkout main or git switch main to return to the present.

(For future questions, and especially those that have a clear technical answer, make sure to pick "Troubleshooting" as the question type, even if one of the others seems right. The other question types activate an experimental question UI that has some major bugs and is not getting fixes.)

Q: How can I know if my app is communicating via VPN? A:

Interface names alone can be false positives: the interface may exist while the tunnel is inactive, and split tunneling may bypass it. Use the platform VPN API and verify an actual request path when possible.

Q: Whether a table with a single attribute primary key is automatically in at least 2NF A:

If relation schema R already is in 1NF and primary key has only one attribute then that relation R at least must be in 2NF.

Q: Extra non-character or empty character or absence is getting printed at the end of target string being matched by regex pattern using find() in java A:

Issue : the last output its giving extra line with an empty character where string is already matched till last character at index 42 , its printing unnecessary printing extra index of 43 , any thoughts on this ?

At the top level, your regex consists of a capturing group quantified by *. The * matches zero or more repetitions, so the overall regex matches empty strings. After it matches the substring "5000tag%!5000tag%!5000tag%!" at [14,41), it successfully matches an empty string at [41,41). When any matcher matches an empty string, it advances its position by one to avoid matching the same empty string again, so that happens here. Then it matches another empty string between the q and the 1 at [42,42), and finally, one after the 1, at the end of the string, [43,43).

43 is a valid index into your 43-character targetString, as you can verify with targetString.substring(43) or targetString.substring(43, 43), both of which will successfully return an empty string.

Generally speaking, * is often useful in regexes, but only very rarely do you want a whole regex that can match an empty string. You can adjust your regex to fix that by changing the quantifier from * to + (matches one or more repetitions of the quantified subexpression). Or since you're stepping through the target string with find(), perhaps you don't want any quantifier at all.

Additionally, you might want to know about the bracketed quantifiers {n}, {n,m}, etc. These can be much cleaner than literal repeats for matching specific subexpression counts, easier both to write and to read. For example:

String regex = "((\\d{4})(\\w{3})(\\W{2}))+";

Q: JUnit Test cases failing after upgrading to Gradle 9, Springboot 4 and Java 25 A:

Change spring-boot-starter-web to spring-boot-starter-webmvc.

Use spring-boot-starter-webmvc-test for the tests for MVC.

Execute

 -./gradlew dependencyInsight --dependency spring-web --configuration testRuntimeClasspath

Q: Error npm exited with non-zero code: 1 expo React Native A:

I was also facing the same issue with my Expo/EAS build.

In my case, it was caused by dependency version mismatches in package.json and package-lock.json.

I fixed it by running:


rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json

npm install

npx expo install

After that, the build worked fine.
